# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## The grading contract: `hard_no_recalc` makes a formula unscoreable (measured on the 40 baseline traces)

This run uses `SPREADSHEETBENCH_SCORING=hard` with `SPREADSHEETBENCH_REWARD_RECALC=0`. The grader
reads **stored cell values** and never recalculates. openpyxl writes a formula as `<f>` with **no
`<v>`**, so a formula cell reads back as **empty** and can never match — however correct it is.

- **Confirmed by direct measurement of the baseline (pre-RESULT, from the traces themselves, not a
  guess):** tasks whose solution code writes formulas pass **0 of 13**; tasks that write literals
  pass **18 of 27**. Seven failing tasks (37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942) carry
  `test_case_results=[1]` alongside `test_case_results_no_recalc=[0]` — they solved the spreadsheet
  problem and lost only on the stored-value contract.
- **Refuted:** "the instruction wording tells you when a formula is wanted." 3 of 4 sampled
  *passing* tasks also ask for "a formula". Wording is not a discriminator, so the compute-in-Python
  rule must be unconditional.
- **Refuted:** "the `#N/A` cluster is input NaN propagated through." 54144 and 37456 never read a
  value from the input (no `data_only=True` in either trace); the error tokens come from evaluating
  the agent's own defective formula (Excel-365-only `TEXTSPLIT`; a `$A$2` anchor where the header is
  on row 3). The fix is "your logic is wrong", not "don't propagate".
- Awaiting a RESULT for cand_0001 to confirm the prose fix converts these.

## Verification is the second-largest lever, and it was structurally discouraged

- **Measured:** **39 of 40** baseline traces never re-opened the file they wrote. The single trace
  that did (416-15) passed. The agent read `[Code executed successfully with no output]` as success.
- **Mechanism found:** when `task_template.md` is absent the adapter uses its built-in
  `_TASK_TEMPLATE`, which contains *"once that file exists, you are done"*. Creating
  `task_template.md` at all is what suppresses that line. A future iteration that deletes the file
  brings the line back.
- **Corollary, measured:** the freed budget is already there. 46897 resubmitted a byte-identical
  block 28×, 6698 29×, 55049 27× — the wasted rounds exceed an audit's cost tenfold. The missing
  pieces were a stop condition and a defined next action, not turns.
- **Verified constraint on any audit snippet:** 5 of the 18 passing tasks have legitimately blank
  gold cells (382-10 79% — its task *is* to delete values; 395-36 67%; 402-43 65%; 142-12 40%;
  560-12 33% padding). Treating blank as a defect false-alarms on exactly those 5. Blank must be a
  judgement ("is a value expected here?"), never a reflex, and the prose must forbid padding a range
  to look full.
- Also verified: an unbounded audit print floods context (1280 lines on 9569, ~4451 cells on 48921).
  Cap the sample and print an aggregate count.

## Two mechanical facts about this adapter worth not rediscovering

- `spreadsheet_content` is `pandas.read_excel(..., header=0)`: the preview's **column labels are
  Excel row 1**, and preview row `i` is **Excel row `i + 2`**. 59196 read `ws["D1"]` (blank, its
  header is row 2) and wrote `None` everywhere; 227-40's `iloc[13]` landed on Excel row 15,
  producing exactly its observed 12/20.
- `extract_code` takes only the **FIRST** ```python block in a reply; the rest are silently
  discarded. 46897's opening reply had 6 blocks, so its diagnostic `print`s never ran and it
  resolved a genuine ambiguity by speculation.
- `openpyxl.utils.range_boundaries` **rejects a sheet-qualified range** — split on `!` and strip
  quotes before calling it. `openpyxl`'s `ArrayFormula` is neither `str` nor numeric, so a
  `startswith("=")` check misses it while an `isinstance` type check catches it.
- An **empty** `prompt.md` means "no system message"; a **missing** one falls back to
  `_DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`. The two are not equivalent.
- 402-43 passes while its pandas round trip **silently drops Sheet1** — grading was confined to
  Sheet2. A latent fragility, not a real pass of the whole workbook.
